literal: If they see, water-lilies having bowed down ground will look, "excellent-jewels' eyes we do not equal" saying.
translation: If water-lilies could see, they would bow their heads and look at the ground, saying, "We cannot equal the eyes of this woman wearing excellent jewels."
modern: குவளை மலர்கள் காணும் திறன் பெற்றிருந்தால், "இந்தச் சிறந்த அணிகலன்களை அணிந்தவளின் கண்களுக்கு நாங்கள் ஒப்பாக மாட்டோம்" என்று நாணிக் தலைகவிழ்ந்து நிலத்தைப் பார்க்கும்.
explanation: The speaker praises the beauty of the woman's eyes by comparing them to water-lilies, a classic poetic standard for beautiful eyes. He imagines that if the flowers were granted the power of sight, they would realize their own inferiority. Overcome with modesty and shame at the realization that they cannot match the beauty of the woman's eyes, the water-lilies would bow their heads and stare at the ground. The word 'மாணிழை' (excellent jewels) is used as a metonymy to refer to the woman herself.
